sites.label: A
sites.name_ja: Almaty regional HQ (Esentai Tower, Al-Farabi Avenue)
sites.coord_note_ja: Nominatim way 1458250144 'Esentai Tower Business Center, 77/7 Al-Farabi Avenue' (43.2193,76.9293); Wikipedia 43.21905,76.92937
sites.building_ja: Esentai Tower, Al-Farabi Avenue 77/7: 36-storey, 162 m reinforced-concrete office/hotel tower completed 2008 (offices on floors 1-14, Ritz-Carlton above, LEED Silver 2016; Wikipedia). Office assumed on the 12th floor; standby generator serves common areas only (assumption)
sites.desc_ja: On Al-Farabi Avenue at the southern, upslope edge of the city center (Bostandyk district, about 870 m), next to the channelized Esentai river and 1.5 km west of the Kishi Almaty mudflow corridor. Almaty was destroyed by earthquakes in 1887 and 1911 (M8.0 Kemin, 37 km away) and lost about 500 people to the 1921 Kishi Almaty mudflow; the Medeu dam stopped the 1973 flow, and on 23 July 2015 a glacial-lake outburst mudflow hit the western outskirts (900 evacuated). The M7.0 Wushi earthquake of 22 January 2024 (270 km away) was felt in the city's high-rises with USGS community intensity 4.6 from 235 Almaty reports (USGS us7000lsze).
sites.risk_note_ja: ThinkHazard: earthquake High, landslide Medium, extreme heat Medium, wildfire High, river/urban flood Very low. For this tower the governing risks are strong shaking (design intensity MSK-64 9) with long elevator outages and facade/glass damage, winter smog and heavy snow, and mudflow risk confined to the river corridors east and west of the site rather than the building itself.

sites.flood_trigger_ja: Mudflow (sel) is a warning-led hazard: when KazSelezaschita / the Almaty Department for Emergency Situations issue a mudflow warning for the Kishi or Ulken Almaty basins or a Medeu dam alert (typically June-August after heat waves or heavy rain), staff living in Gorny Gigant and within 300 m of the Kishi Almaty, Esentai or Ulken Almaty channels move to pre-agreed high ground away from the rivers (Republic Square, KazNU campus) by car or on foot without crossing river bridges; the Esentai office itself lies outside the corridors and switches to remote work. sites.label: B
sites.name_ja: Atyrau branch office and logistics base (Bayterek Plaza, west bank)
sites.type_ja: Oil & gas services branch office and logistics base
sites.building_ja: Bayterek Plaza business centre, 25 Student (Studenchesky) Ave, west bank, about 450 m from the Zhaiyk embankment and 500 m south-west of the Central Bridge (OSM office building, Nominatim page_read). Floors, structure and year not verified - assumed 6-storey reinforced-concrete frame, 2010s; office on the 4th floor, yard and warehouse assumed in the Nursaya-3 industrial strip on the airport road.
sites.desc_ja: West-bank business district between Satpayev Street and the river, 450 m south of Tengizchevroil's head office (3 Satpayev St), 500 m from the regional akimat (seat of the regional flood operations staff) and 200 m from the Marriott Executive Apartments. In the record spring flood of 2024 the Atyrau gauge exceeded its critical level (553 cm vs 550 cm, mid-May) but the embankments held and the centre stayed dry; the site's exposure was indirect - staff whose families lived in flooded Kulsary (33,641 evacuated, April 2024), floodplain dacha evacuations, bridge and road restrictions and the use of the Tengiz rotation camps for evacuees.
sites.risk_note_ja: River flood High (ThinkHazard) but with weeks of lead time from the upstream gauges (Uralsk critical 850 cm, Atyrau 550 cm); urban ponding during the spring thaw; earthquake Very low. Extreme heat Medium (record 44.6 C) and severe winter cold (record -37.9 C) make power and heating continuity critical; hydrogen-sulfide air-pollution episodes; dependence on two road bridges, one airport (GUW) and the Atyrau-Kulsary-Tengiz road for the logistics chain.

sites.flood_trigger_ja: Zhaiyk floods are forecast weeks ahead. Triggers: Kazhydromet forecast of the Atyrau gauge approaching its 550 cm critical level (2024 peak 553 cm) or the Uralsk gauge passing 850 cm; MES/akimat evacuation orders for floodplain dachas, Balykshi or Zhumysker; a dike-breach report (as at Sokolok on 24 May 2024); or closure of the Central or Sultan Beibarys bridge. On trigger, move staff and families by vehicle to the west-bank office/hotel cluster or out by air (GUW) before roads are cut; walking routes are a last resort.

sites.label: C
sites.name_ja: Tashkent country office (Nest One, Tashkent City)
sites.coord_note_ja: Wikipedia infobox coord 41.3121,69.2519; Nominatim way 878651866 'Nest One, 1A/1 Yangi Toshkent ko'chasi, Tashkent City' 41.31208,69.25195
sites.building_ja: Nest One, 1A/1 Yangi Toshkent Street, Tashkent City International Business Center: 51-storey, 266.5 m mixed-use tower (offices, apartments, hotel, retail; 34 elevators), completed 2022 and opened 2023, the tallest building in Uzbekistan (Wikipedia). Office assumed on the 15th floor; standby generator serves common areas only (assumption)
sites.desc_ja: In the Tashkent City business district on the former Olmazor mahalla site, 600 m north of the Anhor canal and 2 km south-west of the Monument of Courage that marks the epicentre of the 26 April 1966 earthquake, which destroyed the adobe old city just north of here and left 200,000-300,000 people homeless. The district was built 2018-2023 to current seismic codes; recent stresses were the January 2023 cold wave with gas and power shortages, the record-level heat of July 2026 (44.3 C) and the November 2021 dust storm.
sites.risk_note_ja: ThinkHazard (Tashkent city): earthquake High, wildfire High, extreme heat Medium, water scarcity Medium, river/urban flood Low, landslide Low. For this tower the governing risks are strong shaking in seismic zone 8-9 with elevator entrapment and facade damage, summer heat with grid failures and winter gas/power shortages; flood exposure is limited to canal corridors and underpasses away from the site.

sites.districts_note_ja: Populations are the 2021 figures of the Tashkent City statistics department as tabulated on Wikipedia (third_party; sum 2,694,400). The city total was 3,164,030 on 1 October 2025 (Wikipedia infobox, third_party) after registration and boundary changes, so current district figures are about 15-20% higher. District coordinates are the Wikipedia article coordinates (page_read). toshstat.uz and citypopulation.de are blocked in this session.
sites.flood_trigger_ja: Flood is a low, warning-led hazard here: when Uzhydromet issues a heavy-rain or mudflow warning for Tashkent and the Chirchik basin, or the Bozsu-Anhor-Salar canals run full after Charvak releases (March-June), staff living within 150 m of the Anhor or Salar canals avoid basements and underpasses and park cars on high ground; the Nest One office itself (600 m from the Anhor, on a raised podium) is not expected to flood and switches to remote work only if roads are impassable. Procedure is an assumption for the demo.
